question.text: What is the mass ratio of ethylene glycol (<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi><mn>6</mn></msub><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math>, molar mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>=</mo><mn>62</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>mol</mi></math>) required for making <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>500</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math> of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>25</mn></math> molal aqueous solution and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>250</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mL</mi></math> of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>25</mn></math> molar aqueous solution?

solution.text:
The molality of aqueous ethylene glycol solution = 0.25 m

Mass of ethylene glycol required for 1000 g water = 624 = 15.5 gm

Mass of solution = 1015.5 gm

Mass of ethylene glycol in 500 gm solution = 15.5 × 5001015.5 = 7.63 gm

Assuming density of solution as 1 gm/mL.

Mass of ethylene glycol in 250 mL =7.632 = 3.815 gm

Mass ratio of ethylene glycol for making 500 gm of 0.25 m solution and 250 mL of 0.25 m solution = 2 : 1

So, the correct option is C
